subject: amateur sommeliers
one_liner: Drag-and-drop tasting notes for people who swirl with intent and mostly taste grape.
brand_voice_notes: Legs talks like a wine-bar menu that got a Series A. Hushed, confident, faintly French, never sure what minerality is. It treats a tasting note as a design asset, the wine as optional input, and the user's palate as a brand to be kept on-message. Nobody at Legs admits the product writes the note for you. It 'composes alongside you'.

hero.h1: Describe the wine before you taste it.
hero.sub: Legs is a design platform for amateur sommeliers. Pick a template, drop in three adjectives, and serve a tasting note that sounds like it cost more than the bottle.

features.title: 4,200 tasting-note templates
features.blurb: Every note a professional has ever written, sorted by how confident you want to sound. Wet slate. Forest floor after a light argument. A whisper of pencil shavings. Drag one onto the page and nod slowly.

features.title: Palate Brand Kit
features.blurb: Choose five signature descriptors and Legs applies them to every wine you drink, including the ones that came in a box. A palate is mostly consistency. Ours is locked.

features.title: Label Glow-Up
features.blurb: Photograph a $9 bottle. Legs adds a crest, a château and the word Réserve in gold foil. The wine is unchanged. Your guests are not told.

testimonials.quote: I used to say 'this one's nice'. Now I say 'bright acidity with a long, apologetic finish' and people stop talking to me, respectfully.
testimonials.name: Denise Harrowgate
testimonials.title: Hosts Wine Night Every Second Friday, Attendance Declining

testimonials.quote: I made a tasting note for tap water. My brother-in-law asked where he could buy it.
testimonials.name: Marcus Oyelaran
testimonials.title: Owns Four Corkscrews, Uses One

testimonials.quote: The Brand Kit gave me cedar, tension, graphite, rain and restraint. I have not had a drink since that didn't fit.

demo_screen_concept: The Legs editor, a Canva-style workspace for a single tasting-note card. Left rail has three tabs (Descriptors, Templates, Glass). Descriptors is a searchable, category-filtered library of chips (Fruit, Earth, Emotional, Expensive) such as 'wet slate', 'forest floor after a light argument', 'a hint of barnyard'; clicking a chip places it on the card and clicking it on the card removes it. Templates swaps the card layout between Cellar Card, Menu Column and Chalkboard. Glass recolors an SVG wine glass on the card across seven hues from 'rosé-adjacent' to 'inky, frankly'. A right-hand inspector shows a live Pretension meter and a Believability meter that fall in opposite directions as descriptors are added, plus a Swirl button that animates the glass and a Present to Table button that opens the note full-screen in a modal.

images.rationale: Candlelit editorial direction asks for one still-life in the hero, so 1 hero. The demo is a design-tool canvas with an SVG glass, which is not photo-shaped, so no demo assets. Remaining budget of 3 goes to testimonial headshots.

items.prompt: Editorial still-life photograph, low candlelight. A single stemmed wine glass of deep claret red wine (#7B1E2B) on a dark oxblood-black tabletop, near-black background (#1A1113), warm gold candle glow (#C9A45C) rim-lighting the glass from the left, visible wine legs. Glass right of center, dark negative space left. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no bottles, no rendered UI screens.

Deadpan corporate headshot of a woman in her late 50s holding a glass of red wine near her face with an over-composed expression. Dark oxblood backdrop (#2A1A1C), parchment blouse (#F1E6D6). No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.

Deadpan corporate headshot of a Black man in his 40s in a navy blazer holding a corkscrew at chest height with complete seriousness. Dark oxblood backdrop (#2A1A1C), faint gold rim light (#C9A45C). No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.

Deadpan corporate headshot of a South Asian woman in her 30s mid-sniff over a wine glass, one hand raised asking for silence. Dark oxblood backdrop (#2A1A1C), claret sweater (#7B1E2B). No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.

design_direction.style: Candlelit wine-list editorial, cellar dark mode. The page is staged as the leather-bound wine list of a restaurant that is slightly too proud of itself: near-black oxblood ground, parchment type, gold-foil hairline rules and dotted menu leaders between every name and price. One dark mode only, the first dark entry in over a week. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: ruled worksheets, reward stickers, red pen, highlighter swipes, large-print sliders, glossy 8x10s, staples, applause signs, SMPTE bars, pegboard, aisle signs, shelf tags, cork, push pins, tape, bites, pulp cells, grade stamps, vent holes, vinyl bladders, valves, weld seams. Also absent: glassmorphism, blur, neon, gradients behind body text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The menu leader: every label-to-value pair (tier name to price, wine to vintage, stat to figure) is joined by a dotted leader in muted gold. (2) The foil rule: section dividers are a double gold hairline, 1px and 1px with a 3px gap, centered with a small diamond. (3) The pour: primary CTA and the highlighted tier are solid claret #7B1E2B with parchment text, square corners, and a 1px gold inner keyline. (4) The legs: a few thin vertical streaks of translucent claret run down the hero's right edge, the way wine runs down the inside of a glass. Headings are Gloock, large, sentence case, tight. Body is Hanken Grotesk 17px/1.65. Every price, vintage and score is Fragment Mono with tabular figures.
design_direction.archetype: Hero-centric SaaS landing: full-height hero with product still-life, value strip, three features, testimonials, pricing as a wine list, closing CTA.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Slow pours. Sections fade up 10px on reveal (gated behind a .js class with a timeout fallback), the hero legs streak down once over 1.6s, buttons darken and their gold keyline brightens on hover in 200ms, the demo glass swirls with a 700ms rotate-and-settle. All motion off under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns on desktop. Left: small gold eyebrow 'Legs · design for the palate', a huge Gloock h1 across three lines, the sub, a claret CTA and a quiet text link to the demo. Right: a tall candlelit still-life photo of a single glass of red, framed by a thin gold keyline with a mono caption plate beneath ('Fig. 1 · A $9 wine, described'). On mobile the photo stacks under the copy.
